question: What are the required documents for the pre-assessment of a new business permit in Davao City?
reference_answer:
For NEW business permit pre-assessment, the charter lists the following requirements. Apply the ownership, representation, vehicle and activity conditions stated in each row. Source: Business Bureau printed pages 41-42 (PDF pages 2-3). These transcribed rows include their Where to Secure entries.

1. Duly filled-out Unified Application Form (1 original) Business Bureau or at the Web site https://busbureau.davaocity.gov.ph/ or apply online at https://appbts.davaocity.gov.ph/
2. Sketch / Google map of Business location (1 original) with pictures of the premise location Applicant
3. Certified List of Employees / Certification of no Employee (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. Valid DTI Registration for Single Proprietorship (1 photocopy) Department of Trade and Industry
5. SEC Registration, Articles of Incorporation for Partnership and Corporation (1 photocopy) Securities and Exchange Commission
6. Certificate of Cooperation, Articles of Cooperation for Cooperative (1 photocopy). Cooperative Development Authority
7. DOLE / POEA Certificate of Registration, if applicable. Department of Labor and Employment
8. DHSUD Certificate of Registration, if applicable. Department of Human Settlement and Urban Development
9. Special Power of Attorney (1 current and original) for represented – Sole Proprietorship Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
10. Partnership Resolution (1 current and original) for represented – Partnership Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
11. Secretary’s Certificate or Board Resolution for other form of ownership (1 current and original) - Corporation and Cooperative Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
12. Valid I.D. of representatives, owners (Sole Proprietor, OPC, Partnership), and Corporate Secretary (Corporation, Cooperative) - 1 photocopy each) Applicant
13. Contract of Lease and copy of the Proof of ownership by the Lessor if business location is not owned and is rented by the applicant (1 photocopy) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
14. Any proof of ownership if Business location is owned Applicant
15. consent and copy of any proof of ownership if business location is not owned and is freely used by the applicant (1 photocopy) Applicant
16. OR/CR of vehicle, if with delivery vehicle (1 photocopy each vehicle) Applicant
17. Consent for use of the vehicle if not owned by the applicant. Applicant
18. FSIC for Occupancy Permit valid in the last 9 months Bureau of Fire Protection
19. Affidavit of Undertaking that there had been no substantial changes made on the building Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
20. Other Requirements depending on the Business Activity declared Concerned Agency

question: Sino ang kailangang kumuha ng Occupational Permit, magkano ang bayad, at magkano ang penalty kapag late nag-renew?
reference_answer:
According to the Occupational Permit section of the thesis source charter (printed pages 104-106; PDF pages 65-67):

The charter states that an Occupational Permit is issued to any worker or employee who is not a holder of validly issued Professional Tax Receipts, whether working on a temporary or permanent basis.

Under Who may avail, it lists Filipino employees or workers aged 18 at application; foreigners may apply after securing an Alien Employment Permit from DOLE. Where the law allows a person below 18 to work, an Affidavit of Consent from the parent or guardian is required.

Renew annually on or before January 31. The charter states a 25% penalty for late renewal.

The fee table and TOTAL row state PHP 125.00 for new and updated renewal, and PHP 156.25 for late renewal. Payment is to the City Treasurer’s Office.

Application Form: Business Bureau Office, Window 1 or Public Assistance Desk. Certificate of Employment: applicant.

Checklist item 3 specifies Official Receipt (for service crew), from the City Treasurer’s Office. Separately, the process instructs walk-in applicants to submit required documents including the official receipt.

A notarized Affidavit of Consent is listed for minors below 18. For Night Clubs and related establishments and similar places of amusement, the affidavit is listed for ages 18 to 20.

Additional requirements for Entertainers, Masseurs, Bar Attendants: Birth Certificate (Philippine Statistics Authority); Valid ID of parent or qualified guardian for parent’s consent with appearance (Where to Secure: Any Notary public); Health ID (City Health).

The process note states: If the applicant is an entertainer, masseur, or bar attendant 18-20 years old, or the applicant is below 18 years old, he or she must present himself/herself for an interview. Agency action 2.2 repeats these conditions.

The charter states that an Occupational Permit is issued to any worker or employee who is not a holder of validly issued Professional Tax Receipts, whether working on a temporary or permanent basis.

Under Who may avail, it lists Filipino employees or workers aged 18 at application; foreigners may apply after securing an Alien Employment Permit from DOLE. Where the law allows a person below 18 to work, an Affidavit of Consent from the parent or guardian is required.

Renew annually on or before January 31. The charter states a 25% penalty for late renewal.

The fee table and TOTAL row state PHP 125.00 for new and updated renewal, and PHP 156.25 for late renewal. Payment is to the City Treasurer’s Office.

Application Form: Business Bureau Office, Window 1 or Public Assistance Desk. Certificate of Employment: applicant.

Checklist item 3 specifies Official Receipt (for service crew), from the City Treasurer’s Office. Separately, the process instructs walk-in applicants to submit required documents including the official receipt.

A notarized Affidavit of Consent is listed for minors below 18. For Night Clubs and related establishments and similar places of amusement, the affidavit is listed for ages 18 to 20.

Additional requirements for Entertainers, Masseurs, Bar Attendants: Birth Certificate (Philippine Statistics Authority); Valid ID of parent or qualified guardian for parent’s consent with appearance (Where to Secure: Any Notary public); Health ID (City Health).

The process note states: If the applicant is an entertainer, masseur, or bar attendant 18-20 years old, or the applicant is below 18 years old, he or she must present himself/herself for an interview. Agency action 2.2 repeats these conditions.

reference_answer:

1. Submit requirements for pre-assessment, receive and sign the retirement application, then proceed to the City Treasurer’s Office for assessment of dues and approval for retirement.

3. Receive the retired business permit and the applicant’s copies of required documents; the processing staff receives the claim stub and releases them.

question: Kanus-a required magpasa ug FSCR, FSCCR, ug FSMR sa BFP ug kinsa ang licensed practitioner nga pwede magpirma?
reference_answer: FSCR/FSCCR/FSMR are required if the building/facilities/structures are required to install any or a combination of wet standpipe, automatic fire suppression, or automatic fire detection and alarm systems. FSCR consists of plans, specifications and design analysis per building, prepared and duly signed by the Engineer/Architect-of-Record and his/her Fire Safety Practitioner. FSCCR compiles approved submittals, test and acceptance forms for fire protection and life safety features as part of as-built documents turned over by the contractor to the owner; it is duly signed by the Contractor/Construction Manager and his/her Fire Safety Practitioner. FSMR is prepared by the building owner, his/her fire safety practitioner or authorized representative, and duly signed by the Building Administrator and his/her Fire Safety Practitioner during regular annual fire safety inspection. The matrix associates FSCR with FSEC, FSCCR with occupancy FSIC, and FSMR with new business without valid occupancy-stage FSIC and the two renewal columns; blank cells are not exemption statements.

question: Unsa ang mga plano, pirma sa inhinyero ug clearances nga kailangan i-submit para makakuha ug building permit sa OCBO?
reference_answer:
The Building Permit checklist lists a notarized application letter; notarized Unified Building Permit Form with Civil/Architectural plans signed/sealed by a licensed Civil Engineer/Architect (5 accomplished form copies); Architectural, Civil/Structural, and Sanitary/Plumbing forms (3 form copies and 5 plan sets each). Civil/Structural plans identify a licensed Civil Engineer; Sanitary/Plumbing identifies a licensed Sanitary Engineer/Master Plumber. Architectural plans must be signed/sealed by the hired licensed professional.

Electrical: 3 accomplished form copies and 5 plan sets, signed/sealed by a Licensed Professional Electrical Engineer. Electronics: 2 form copies and 5 plan sets, signed/sealed by a Licensed Electronics Engineer. Mechanical row states "Mechanical Permit Form with 6-7 sets Mechanical Plans" signed and sealed by the hired professional "Licensed Electronics Engineer"; it separately lists "2 copies of accomplished Form" and "5 sets of plans". These are preserved as separate source statements. The user interprets the latter five sets as another submission; the row does not explicitly say additional or specify a combined total.

The checklist also lists Zoning Location Clearance and BFP Fire Safety Evaluation Certificate (1 original and 1 photocopy each); certified true copies of land title, property tax declaration and current real-property-tax receipt (1 original and 1 photocopy each); owner/applicant ID with 3 specimen signatures (1 photocopy); PRC IDs, current PTR and TIN of signing professionals (1 photocopy per professional).

Other listed technical submissions include scaled sketch/lot and vicinity plans, relocation survey plans/reports signed/sealed by a licensed Geodetic Engineer (4 copies); technical specifications signed/sealed by a licensed Architect (2 copies); bill of materials/cost estimates signed/sealed by a licensed Architect (4 copies); seismic analysis; clear detailed location photographs with landmarks or Google Maps image.

Additional clearances are conditional: DPWH for structures along a National Highway; CAAP for tall structures; DENR ECC for environmentally critical projects; drainage clearance where stated; traffic impact assessment with site development/parking plans for major development; and RROW clearance for structures along City/Barangay/Subdivision roads. These rows list 1 original and 1 photocopy and preserve their stated conditions.

The Building Permit checklist lists a notarized application letter; notarized Unified Building Permit Form with Civil/Architectural plans signed/sealed by a licensed Civil Engineer/Architect (5 accomplished form copies); Architectural, Civil/Structural, and Sanitary/Plumbing forms (3 form copies and 5 plan sets each). Civil/Structural plans identify a licensed Civil Engineer; Sanitary/Plumbing identifies a licensed Sanitary Engineer/Master Plumber. Architectural plans must be signed/sealed by the hired licensed professional.

Electrical: 3 accomplished form copies and 5 plan sets, signed/sealed by a Licensed Professional Electrical Engineer. Electronics: 2 form copies and 5 plan sets, signed/sealed by a Licensed Electronics Engineer. Mechanical row states "Mechanical Permit Form with 6-7 sets Mechanical Plans" signed and sealed by the hired professional "Licensed Electronics Engineer"; it separately lists "2 copies of accomplished Form" and "5 sets of plans". These are preserved as separate source statements. The user interprets the latter five sets as another submission; the row does not explicitly say additional or specify a combined total.

The checklist also lists Zoning Location Clearance and BFP Fire Safety Evaluation Certificate (1 original and 1 photocopy each); certified true copies of land title, property tax declaration and current real-property-tax receipt (1 original and 1 photocopy each); owner/applicant ID with 3 specimen signatures (1 photocopy); PRC IDs, current PTR and TIN of signing professionals (1 photocopy per professional).

Other listed technical submissions include scaled sketch/lot and vicinity plans, relocation survey plans/reports signed/sealed by a licensed Geodetic Engineer (4 copies); technical specifications signed/sealed by a licensed Architect (2 copies); bill of materials/cost estimates signed/sealed by a licensed Architect (4 copies); seismic analysis; clear detailed location photographs with landmarks or Google Maps image.

Additional clearances are conditional: DPWH for structures along a National Highway; CAAP for tall structures; DENR ECC for environmentally critical projects; drainage clearance where stated; traffic impact assessment with site development/parking plans for major development; and RROW clearance for structures along City/Barangay/Subdivision roads. These rows list 1 original and 1 photocopy and preserve their stated conditions.

question: What is the fee and requirement checklist to request a Certified True Copy of a lost Building Permit at OCBO?
reference_answer:
For a Certified True Copy, submit request letter; photocopy of Building Permit and other related documents; owner valid-ID photocopy with 3 signatures; if not owner, processor valid-ID photocopy with 3 signatures and original SPA; if lost, original Affidavit of Loss. The checklist does not offer reference details as a substitute for the photocopy.

Pay PHP50 per document (1 copy) at the City Treasurer’s Office. The printed TOTAL is 2 Days, 1 Hour, and 19 Minutes. Preserve this as the source-listed total, not an independently verified sum: listed steps include two separate 3-hour entries plus 2 days and other minutes.

question: Ano ang karagdagang requirements ng OCBO kapag ang itatayong gusali ay may 3 floors pataas?
reference_answer: Conditional requirements state: construction/minor repair of buildings 3 storeys and above requires Construction Safety & Health Program, 1 original and 1 photocopy, with DOLE listed under Where to Secure. Boring and Plate Load Test Result/Report is listed if the structure is at least three storeys, 2 copies, with a licensed Civil/Geotechnical Engineer listed. For an additional storey, submit an affidavit that the foundation can carry the proposed additional floors, 2 originals.
